families.access: P14: tenant access, membership and encrypted credentials; distinct from platform authority
families.activity: P21: tenant activity and health facts, indexes and bounded projections
families.analytics: P22: typed analytics, prepared queries, retained samples, durable usage and cost reporting
families.artifact-service: External artifact service catalog and object bytes; P17/P25 must preserve reachability and integrity
families.billing: P15: tenant plans, immutable credit ledgers, budgets and billing receipts
families.board: P07: tenant board, page and saved-view contracts under the core unit-of-work
families.claim: P11: claim, admission, recovery and completion facts on the core/event/lease transaction
families.collaboration: P17: tenant threads, unread state, attachment/artifact references and operator chat
families.conversation: P16: tenant conversation messages, commands, tools and content references
families.conversion: P25: storageconversion plus remaining archive/conversion/reclaim owners and durable cursors
families.core: P04-P06: extend tenant corestore unit-of-work for projects, issues, comments, relationships and numbering
families.delivery: P20: tenant notification subscriptions, delivery queues and uncertain external-write receipts
families.event: P08: eventstore and immutable Change versions on the shared tenant transaction
families.fleet: P12-P13: tenant runner enrollment, identity, routing, placement and capacity contracts
families.lease: P10: leasestore machine, lease, run and attempt records on the shared tenant transaction
families.lifecycle: P03/P25: backend startup, schema authority, identity, backup and database plumbing
families.local-runtime: Outside Hub port: #2022 runner/local CLI/board SQLite and developer diagnostics stay local
families.metrics: P23: metricsstore retained request grains, histograms and background retention
families.non-storage: Conservative source-scan match to URL/query, process, UI text or preparation APIs; no SQL execution
families.platform: P26: platformstore; registry/auth owners switch together under one global authority
families.policy: P19: tenant policy revisions, integrations, onboarding and GitHub import/webhook receipts
families.search: P24: tenant PostgreSQL approximate search and bounded index refresh; preserve searchable source content
families.source: P09: source custody, landing, attribution, outbox and test/release receipts under the event transaction
families.workspace: P18: tenant workspace sessions, actions, relay tickets and terminal references

change-publication.contract: Each Change/publication command atomically checks revision and source authority, writes immutable version/evidence/receipt and linked issue/history/command result. Source custody and uncertain external publication receipts remain durable. Git/object/network work occurs outside the database transaction and reconciles by stable receipt/ref.

claim.contract: One claim transaction revalidates current authorization, intent, dependency, policy, capacity and fence; allocates lease/session and reservations; records attempt/scheduler history and progress. Candidate preflight uses a separate read snapshot and grants no ownership. Roll back every participant when any step fails; prepare objects before the writer transaction.

completion.contract: Ordered run.finished and prior events use the native command transaction. Validate current run/session/fencing token and revision, update attempt and issue/dependency state, publication metadata, usage accounting, immutable history and command receipt together. Rejected/stale completion commits none; duplicate receipt does not charge or publish twice. Run payload bytes and stable object references are staged in the same command transaction before external upload. Separate publication transactions recheck current lease authority and clear pending bytes only after verifying the published object; conversion can resume publication from the durable staged bytes.

conversation-command.contract: Commit each conversation mutation, revision/sequence, command receipt and linked issue metadata in its owning transaction. Publication plans prepare immutable payload objects before commit and reconcile external actions afterward. Do not nest a core repository callback or independently commit a linked family.

conversion-publication.contract: Prepare and verify immutable object bytes outside the writer, then atomically publish source-bound metadata/object references and conversion progress. Discovery is a separate bounded transaction. Restart from durable cursor without exposing an unverified object or discarding authoritative history.

lease-lifecycle.contract: Renew, release and event append are distinct invocations, each with one transaction. Validate the current lease/fence before mutation; keep lease release, attempt cancellation, reservation/accounting cleanup and relevant history within that invocation. An expired or replaced worker cannot publish current state.

work-item-command.contract: Work item and comment commands prepare immutable content outside the writer. Project-scoped numbering, revision fences, current core rows, aggregate events, immutable versions and native command receipts commit in one tenant transaction. Comment sequence checks and archive lease reads share that transaction. Relationship mutations lock the tenant graph before endpoint projects, then commit typed edges or labels, revisions, immutable versions, events and command receipts together; cycle checks see the preceding committed graph. Failure publishes no partial database state.

native-command.contract: A native command rechecks current authority and revision, executes its callback, appends immutable history and stores its idempotent result in one transaction. A failed callback writes neither result nor partial state. Object preparation/hydration stays outside the writer; replay returns the prior receipt without another mutation.

outbox.contract: Claim and completion are separate bounded outbox transactions. Queue insertion commits with its initiating state mutation; delivery happens outside the database and the stable key/receipt governs replay, uncertainty and completion.

platform-oauth.contract: Within the auth store, consume the authorization code or rotate/spend the refresh token and persist the resulting credential atomically. Recheck session/client/resource/revocation authority; concurrent replay cannot mint another usable token. Registry and auth are separate SQLite stores, not one cross-database transaction.

platform-provisioning.contract: Commit organization generation, requested intent and corresponding registry event together under the registry transaction. External provisioning happens after commit and resumes from receipts. Auth revocation is a separate auth-store transaction; retain this durable reconciliation boundary during the all-owner platform switch.

platform-session.contract: Each auth mutation has its own transaction for session/binding/revocation/notification state or one-time login consumption. Preserve globally unique credential routing and keyring compatibility. Global backend selection switches every platform owner together; no independent platform owner may retain SQLite after the switch.

postgres-callback.contract: Each existing core/event/lease callback starts its own tenant-bound read-committed transaction with pool budgets and one generated query binding. Separate callbacks are separate commits; nesting or sequencing them does not implement the SQLite claim/completion atomic groups. P02 must expose all participating family operations through one shared session and commit/rollback once.

project-records.contract: Project creation, settings or retirement and the native command receipt share one tenant write scope. Prepare and hydrate payload objects outside it. Claims share the project row against retirement; deletion never releases claims or deletes retained issue history. The access owner retains its authority transaction through the bounded tenant write. Hosted grants, audit, plans, source updates and retirement cleanup enter through required lifecycle participants on that same scope; missing participants refuse the operation without SQLite project writes.

runner-authority.contract: Each runner/admin command owns a separate transaction that revalidates current credential hash, revocation, enrollment and tenant scope, then commits callback state and hosted consumption together. Dispatch notifications follow commit. Preserve fresh authority checks for every heartbeat or mutation.

secret-update.contract: Each authorized secret update commits the encrypted envelope/key version and audit metadata in the same tenant transaction; preserve organization/project binding and fail closed on unavailable keys. Never move tenant secret reads to global platform authority.

thread-post.contract: Each thread creation/post commits its own sequence, post/reference metadata and requested unread refresh together. Background unread advancement is a separate bounded transaction; it is not pulled into the request. Preserve audience authorization and concurrent read cursors.

platform-import.contract: An offline step reads one indexed page from a fenced immutable registry/auth snapshot, prepares and verifies immutable objects outside the target transaction, then commits the source records, directly owned relational children, sequence allocation and typed checkpoint together. Registry and auth remain separate stages. Snapshot/catalog authority is immutable; stale checkpoint revisions and conflicting credentials refuse publication without advancing progress.
